# dist/esm: a declared root's literal import() can still load the source Engine

## Context

Found while reviewing PR #20973 (#20963). With #20973, the ESM build refuses a declared root module whose static edge reaches a helper the build does not emit, when that helper's static graph reaches the Engine. Since #20979 the same check covers `neo.canvasModules` roots as well as `neo.mainAddons`. A dynamic import is no discovery edge (`createEsmBuildPlan()`: "Only imports and re-exports are discovery edges; dynamic imports retain their existing runtime admission"), so this package still builds and loads the source Engine:

- `node_modules/widget/package.json`: `neo: {mainAddons: ['main']}`
- `node_modules/widget/main/Addon.mjs`: `export {load} from '../outside/Helper.mjs';`
- `node_modules/widget/outside/Helper.mjs`: `export const load = () => import('../../neo.mjs/src/core/Base.mjs');`

Probe: the stub-engine workspace of `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs`, built with `buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs`, re-run on 2026-11-15 against `dev`'s build scripts (`73cc04d0f5`). Every case exits 0:

| Case | The emitted root's `load()` returns |
|---|---|
| The package above | `node_modules/neo.mjs/src/core/Base.mjs`, the source Engine |
| The same shape under `neo: {canvasModules: ['canvas']}` | the source Engine |
| A root's own `import('../outside/Helper.mjs')`, where the helper re-exports the Engine | the source Engine |
| A root's own `import('../outside/Helper.mjs')`, where the helper is ordinary | the helper's host copy |

## The Problem

A helper outside every declared root has no runtime admission in `dist/esm`: the emitted root imports it from its host location, and a literal `import()` resolves from there. That is the second Engine graph #20963 closes for static edges, and it is open for both root keys.

## The Architectural Reality

- `staticModuleSpecifiers()` (`buildScripts/util/esmDistTransforms.mjs:381`) returns static imports and re-exports only. The same module already reads literal `import()` specifiers for its rewrite (`staticSpecifier()`), and documents why a computed one names no module.
- The refusal is one loop over `rootModules` in `createEsmBuildPlan()` (`buildScripts/util/esmBuildGraph.mjs:216-228`). Each entry is `{key, node}`, and only the remedy text reads the key (`neo.${key}`). It runs after admission and never widens it.
- `learn/guides/fundamentals/MainThreadAddons.md:349-355` states the rule and names this gap: "This check does not inspect dynamic `import()`, even with a literal path". `learn/guides/advanced/CanvasArchitecture.md:143-144` applies the rule to Canvas helpers "as it does for Main-thread addons".

## The Fix

In the refusal only, a literal `import()` counts as an edge: among a root's own edges, and when deciding whether a module reaches the Engine. Nothing is admitted, and discovery stays static. A computed specifier (`import(base + name)`) stays out, since it names no module. The rule covers every root key, so it needs no key filter.

The message names the importer → specifier and the `neo.${key}` remedy | A computed specifier, or a literal one that reaches only ordinary modules, behaves as today: host path, exit 0 | Row 3 | `esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs`: one arm per AC, red on the merge base |
| Discovery and admission (`staticModuleSpecifiers()` and the plan's walk) | `createEsmBuildPlan()`'s JSDoc: dynamic imports keep their runtime admission | Unchanged: a dynamic edge admits or emits no file | — | No | The ordinary-helper arm: the helper stays out of `dist/esm` |
| Package-authoring guides | This ticket | `MainThreadAddons.md:354-355` says that a literal `import()` path is checked and a computed one is not. `CanvasArchitecture.md:143-144` stays true as written | — | Yes | Diff review |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The probe package fails the ESM build, naming the root's importing edge and the `neo.mainAddons` remedy.
- [ ] The same shape under `neo.canvasModules` fails, naming `neo.canvasModules`.
- [ ] A root's own literal `import()` of an outside helper that reaches the Engine fails the same way.
- [ ] A literal `import()` that reaches only ordinary modules keeps its host path, and the build exits 0.
- [ ] A computed dynamic import changes nothing.
- [ ] `MainThreadAddons.md` replaces its "does not inspect dynamic `import()`" sentence with the literal/computed split.

## Out of Scope

App-side dynamic imports; admitting outside-root files; runtime `loadModule` (#20778).
